# References

- [doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1010](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae1010): UniProt, whose published accession grammar (and -n isoform suffix) mzLib matches (UniProt Consortium 2025, NAR)
- [doi:10.1093/nar/gkv1189](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkv1189): RefSeq, whose protein accession prefixes and .n versions mzLib matches (O'Leary et al. 2016, NAR)

# Not yet verified

The spec lists these as open; they are reported, never hidden:

- Whether to split '\|'-joined protein-group accessions before parsing: mzLib does not, so the verb does not either. Splitting is a grouping rule, and it belongs in mzLib if anywhere.
- An isoform or version past int.MaxValue is dropped with no signal while the namespace still reads uniprot or refseq (ProteinAccession.NumberOrNull). Whether mzLib should leave such an accession unrecognized instead is an mzLib question, not raised upstream yet.
- Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.
